text:
The purchaser will likely prevail because an easement appurtenant that is properly recorded automatically passes with the dominant estate to every subsequent owner and survives any temporary merger of title. When the man sold his house, he conveyed both the benefit of the path and the burden on his own land along with it without needing explicit mention in the deed. Consequently, the purchaser holds a valid easement over the man's remaining property, making the barricade an unlawful obstruction.

CONFIDENCE: 95
